newsitem.title: JAPAN: Currencies stabilising as G7 filters through - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Currencies stabilising as G7 filters through - MOF.

text.p: Currencies are becoming stable as the agreement by the Group of Seven (G7) nations on foreign exchange rates reached in Washington last month has filtered through to the markets, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a news conference on Tuesday.
Asked about recent movements in the dollar/yen rate, Mitsuzuka said: "The G7 joint agreement reached in Washington has filtered through and (the rate) is stabilising."

Asked whether the ministry has any plans to change the banking law to strengthen penalties after the troubles at Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd, Mitsuzuka said he was aware of criticisms and that MOF must tackle the issue with a vision of what the appropriate penalties should be.

Mitsuzuka said the government would work towards finalising a plan to reform state finances by the end of May. The ministry would take the government's final report into account when drawing up the state budget for next fiscal year and also prepare bills to carry out the plan, he said.
If the bills were not ready in time for the current parliament session, which ends on June 18, the government might decide to draw up an outline of the bills to be approved by the cabinet.

Asked whether Japan plans to draw up a supplementary budget to subsidise farmers faced with competition due to measures contained in the Uruguay Round trade agreement, Mitsuzuka said MOF would maintain a basic stance that a supplementary budget would be formed only to fund rebuilding from natural disasters and if needed to cover salaries of public employees.

A possible supplementary budget to help farmers is now being debated by the government. Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto has proposed that such an extra budget should be discontinued as part of efforts to cut Japan's fiscal deficit.
